title: Patterns in the Periodic Table
seo_title: Secondary 4 Chemistry: Patterns in the Periodic Table Worksheets (O-Level 6092 with Answers)
standard_code: O-Level Chemistry (6092): Patterns in the Periodic Table
standard_text: Describe the Periodic Table as an arrangement of elements in order of proton number and relate group number to outer electrons; describe the change from metallic to non-metallic character across a period; describe the trends in Group 1 (reactivity, melting point, reaction with water), Group 17 (colour, state, reactivity, displacement) and Group 18; describe the general properties of transition elements; place metals in a reactivity series using their reactions with water, steam and dilute acids and displacement reactions; describe the thermal decomposition of carbonates; relate the extraction of metals to their reactivity; describe rusting and its prevention, including sacrificial protection (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Chemistry 6092 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Chemistry worksheets on patterns in the Periodic Table: Group 1, Group 17, noble gases, transition elements, the reactivity series, extraction of metals and rusting. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Group 1: more reactive down. Group 17: less reactive down.
key_sub: K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb (H) Cu Ag
body_html:
How to think about it

Elements in the same group have similar properties and show trends.

  • Group 1: soft, reactive metals; reactivity increases and melting point decreases down the group; react with water to give an alkali and hydrogen.
  • Group 17: colour darkens and state goes gas → liquid → solid down the group; reactivity decreases; a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one.
  • Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag. Metals above carbon are extracted by electrolysis; below carbon, by reduction with carbon.
  • Rusting needs oxygen and water. Barriers (paint, oil) and sacrificial protection (zinc, magnesium) prevent it.
Example

Does iron displace copper from copper(II) sulfate?

Fe is above Cu

Answer: yes: pink copper forms and the blue colour fades

Example

Does bromine displace chlorine from KCl?

Br₂ is less reactive than Cl₂

Answer: no reaction

Common mistakes

  • Saying Group 1 reactivity decreases down the group.
  • Thinking iodine can displace chlorine.
  • Saying aluminium can be extracted by heating with carbon.
  • Calling painting 'sacrificial protection'.

faq.q: Why does reactivity increase down Group 1?
faq.a: The atoms get larger, so the single outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily.
Metals more reactive than carbon (K to Al) are extracted by electrolysis of their molten compounds; less reactive metals (Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu) by heating their oxides with carbon.
Attaching a more reactive metal such as zinc or magnesium to iron, so the more reactive metal corrodes instead of the iron.
